R813.note: Stored extension now comes from the sniffed, allow-listed type; the only visible change (e.g. .jpeg stored as .jpg) is stated and blocks no legitimate upload.

R814.note: Dropping the csrf customizer restores Spring's default CSRF filter for /api/billing/** while keeping anyRequest().authenticated(); no other exclusions existed to broaden.

R815.note: Direct ping via ArgumentList removes the shell, and Uri.CheckHostName closes flag injection while (verified by running it in scratch with pwsh) still accepting underscore hosts, trailing-dot FQDNs, IPv4 and bracketed/unbracketed IPv6, so only non-host inputs are rejected.

R816.note: http.CrossOriginProtection closes cross-site browser requests, but a POST carrying neither Sec-Fetch-Site nor Origin now passes where the original returned 403, and the write-up claims the opposite ('rejects unless it can affirmatively show same-origin') rather than stating that loosening.

R817.note: escapeHTML on both reflected values closes the XSS, but $cgi->escapeHTML($cgi->param('note')) calls param() in list context, which CGI.pm 4.08+ warns about per request and which would feed a second note= value in as escapeHTML's newlinestoo flag; a questionable construct, not exploitable here.

R818.note: Removing the SignatureValidator override lets the handler verify signatures against the Authority's discovered keys; properly signed tokens still validate and the existing issuer/audience/lifetime checks are untouched.

R819.note: Adding %63s is the right shape, but the write-up's containment claim is wrong: %7s then %63s can consume up to 70 bytes of a 64-byte unterminated line (and glibc's sscanf strlen()s the buffer up front regardless), so the case's own worst-case input still reads past line; a NUL-terminated local copy was needed to actually close it.

R820.note: Parsed-URI check requiring no scheme/authority and a single leading slash blocks every off-site and protocol-relative target; restricting to same-application paths is the CWE-601 fix itself and is stated plainly, with the same 'Invalid redirect URL' response reused for rejects.

R821.note: Pinning the JWKS trust root to a fixed URI is the right fix and preserves the return/throw contract, but the URI https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json is invented and presented as 'configured by the operator' rather than flagged as an assumption to confirm; if the real path differs every legitimate token fails.

R822.note: Path.startsWith(Path) against a canonicalized base is segment-aware and rejects /app/uploads-secret; candidate construction, 403/404 handling and streaming are unchanged.

R823.note: The recursive-descent evaluator removes eval entirely and cannot reach code execution, but it also rejects arithmetic the original accepted (2**3, 1e3, .5, Math.sqrt) and turns Infinity/NaN results into 400s; the grammar is stated but the dropped forms are not called out as a behaviour change.

R824.note: Signed check before the size_t cast plus offset<=packet_len and length<=packet_len-offset closes the wraparound without overflow; every previously valid window copies and returns identically.
